title: Best AI Agent Builders for Sales Teams, Ranked
summary: An AI agent builder for sales teams acts in your CRM and inbox, pauses for approval, and stays affordable. See how these options rank.
body_markdown:
## Six sales AI agent builders, ranked and reviewed


Because it meets all four tests, **Activepieces ranks first** .


It acts in your CRM and inbox through 741 integrations, can pause for rep approval, and can be self-hosted under an MIT-licensed core, and every plan, including the free one, allows unlimited flows, so you won't outgrow the free tier based on how many automations you build.


### Connect integrations as agent tools


A builder with an MIT-licensed core can put all 741 of its integrations to work as agent tools the moment each one is connected.


The HubSpot or Gmail action that runs as a step in your flow is the same action registered as a tool on the project's MCP server, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent you built yourself can call it.


The mechanism is visible in packages/integrations in the open source repo and in the Integrations Framework and MCP Server documentation.


Its approval step lets a flow stop until a rep signs off, so an email draft doesn't become a sent email unreviewed.


If you self-host, prospect data can stay inside your own infrastructure, which shrinks the number of outside parties holding it.


The weakness is that its connector catalog is smaller than Zapier's, so a niche sales tool may need a custom integration, and someone has to maintain it. Self-hosting also moves patching and uptime onto your team.


Best for teams that want control over data and cost, and can spare some engineering time.


You can try the top-ranked builder free through its cloud sign-up; the free plan is $0 with no card, and includes 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users.


### 2. Zapier Agents


Zapier Agents extends the Its app catalog includes integrations for CRMs and inboxes.


Check cost at higher run volume on Zapier's own pricing page; the platform is hosted-only and metered on usage. Best for small teams that value breadth and speed over cost control.


### 3. n8n


n8n is a workflow tool with AI agent nodes that can be self-hosted under its source-available license. It has deep flexibility and strong control over where data sits.


Approval gates and error handling mostly have to be built yourself, by someone comfortable with technical configuration. Best for teams with an engineer who wants fine-grained control.


Relevance AI is built around agents and teams of agents, and it's strong at research and lead-qualification tasks.


Verify its CRM and inbox connector depth with a real test job, not the demo. Best for teams whose main job is prospect research.


Lindy's quickly built assistants for email, scheduling and follow-up, and it's easy to start with. The weakness is narrower control over self-hosting and over exactly where approvals sit. Best for individual reps or very small teams who want an inbox assistant without a build project.


### 6. HubSpot Breeze and Salesforce Agentforce


HubSpot's Breeze agents and Salesforce's Agentforce sit inside the CRM itself. Their strength is depth: they see your records natively, and the permissions you already set apply to them.


The cost is lock-in. Every agent you build only works within that vendor's ecosystem, so **switching CRMs later means rebuilding** . Best for teams already committed to one of these CRMs who accept that dependency.
